articles.title: Selma Blair horrified after being removed from plane for drinking 'too much' before embracing sobriety
articles.summary: Selma Blair is opening up about the "horrifying and humiliating" experience of being taken off an international flight due to drinking "too much."
articles.body: Selma Blair knew she had a problem before she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis: She was self-medicating to ease her pain. But in 2016, she was forced to address the problem after a family vacation ended on a scary note. On a return flight from Cancún, Mexico, to Los Angeles with her son and ex-boyfriend, Jason Bleick, Blair mixed prescription drugs with alcohol. TMZ reported at the time that Blair was crying and saying things like, "He burns my private parts. He won't let me eat or drink," and that she was removed from the aircraft via stretcher and taken to the hospital. Although she made a public apology following the matter, it's only now that Blair says "the plane incident" was her lowest point with alcohol, adding that she had "too much to drink in Mexico." SELMA BLAIR'S MS BATTLE HINDERED HER HOLLYWOOD SUCCESS: 'I COULDN'T EARN MONEY' "I was so messed up and dehydrated and hungover and didn’t know I had neurological issues," Blair told Us Weekly for their new cover story. "I didn’t understand anything. It was horrifying and humiliating. I had to grow up." Days after the original incident, Blair issued an apology to Vanity Fair. "I made a big mistake yesterday. After a lovely trip with my son and his Dad, I mixed alcohol with medication, and that caused me to black out and led me to say and do things that I deeply regret," she said in part. "I am a flawed human being who makes mistakes and am filled with shame over this incident. I am truly very sorry." LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER It ultimately led the actress to get sober — a decision that she says led her to an MS diagnosis — which she shared publicly in 2018. "I wouldn’t have been able to be diagnosed with MS unless I was sober. I wouldn’t be a good mom unless I was sober. I self-medicated," she admitted to Us Weekly. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP Before she had an official name for her condition, Blair says she even questioned whether her pain was real. "I honestly thought I was making it up before I was diagnosed. I just thought, ‘Jesus, Selma, you’re very broken inside. Admit it.’ I didn’t know I wasn’t broken and that I had brain tissue damage," she shared. According to the Cleveland Clinic, multiple sclerosis can "cause muscle weakness, vision changes, numbness and memory issues." Blair has been in remission since 2021.

articles.title: Selma Blair exposes how doctors missed her MS for decades despite clear warning signs
articles.summary: Selma Blair reveals her multiple sclerosis went undiagnosed for decades despite experiencing symptoms since childhood, with doctors dismissing her pain and fatigue.
articles.body: For years, Selma Blair battled unexplained pain and crippling fatigue while doctors dismissed her symptoms.Blair revealed that despite experiencing symptoms since childhood, her multiple sclerosis (MS) wasn’t diagnosed until she was in her 40s. "I was diagnosed with relapsing [remitting] MS in 2018. It turned out I probably had juvenile MS as my first optical neuritis was when I was about seven, which left me with a lazy eye from nerve damage. But there were a lot of things missed my whole life," Blair said at the Flow Space Women’s Health Summit, according to Variety. SELMA BLAIR SAYS SHE'S 'TRULY RELAPSE-FREE' AFTER 7-YEAR BATTLE WITH MS She described years of excruciating pain and countless hospital stays, while doctors brushed off her symptoms. "I had CAT scans as a kid, and I had doctor visits, and I stayed in hospitals for weeks at a time," Blair recalled. "I’d have fevers, I have pain, endless, bone-crushing fatigue that I still do have. And my mom would say, why can’t you give her an MRI?" Blair recalled the double standard she faced growing up, saying, "And they’re like, ‘Oh, she doesn’t need it. She’s probably getting her period.’ But then a boy would come in from my class who had a headache and they gave him an MRI the first thing. Now, they’re not wrong for doing that for him, but it’s like, What? Because I appeared OK, even though I had headaches all the time." SELMA BLAIR EXPLORES MS DIAGNOSIS IN DOCUMENTARY The delayed diagnosis finally explained years of symptoms often dismissed by doctors as mere "growing pains." Blair described how sharing her experience publicly became a source of comfort and connection for many living with chronic illness. "I just put it on my Instagram to thank people on a set who were helping me stay at my job, because I couldn’t use my hands well, I couldn’t take my clothes off. I still sometimes struggle with dystonia and with speech and movement, even though I’m relapse-free right now," Blair continued. LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "But when I did post I saw that there was a whole world that was that felt seen or a part of being seen or could relate to someone having chronic health issues. I realized that was a comfort to a lot of people. And there weren’t a lot of resources out about MS at the time. There was so much I needed to learn. I’m still learning as I live with it, but I did see that it was much bigger than me … It felt good. It felt good knowing people were feeling some comfort." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER The 53-year-old actress, who first announced her MS diagnosis in 2018, revealed in April she is "truly relapse-free" from symptoms of the chronic autoimmune disease. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP "I am doing amazingly well. I’ve been feeling great for about a year," the "Legally Blonde" star told People at the time. "But I am finally well enough to really, genuinely … I always try to feel my best, but now that I actually have stamina and energy and going out isn’t so scary."

articles.title: Jorge Javier Vázquez, tajante sobre las elecciones generales del 29-N: "No dejaría hablar a Feijóo"
articles.standfirst: El presentador se ha pronunciado con un test en su perfil de Instagram
articles.summary: El presentador se ha pronunciado con un test en su perfil de Instagram
articles.body: Las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre continúan generando opiniones al respecto. La última ha sido la del conocido presentador de televisión, Jorge Javier Vázquez, quien se ha pronunciado con un test en su perfil de Instagram. “Buenísima noticia, buenísima noticia por ambos lados”, comenzaba diciendo, asegurando que él votará por correo. Tras ello, el conductor de ‘Supervivientes All Stars’ ha señalado que prefiere no creerse las encuestas, las cuales dicen que Partido Popular y Vox lograrán la mayoría absoluta uniéndose. Además ha confesado que vota lo mismo que su madre y que “se puede, se debe y a veces se tiene que votar con la nariz tapada”. Por otro lado, Jorge Javier ha dejado claro que no solo le parece bien que se hayan convocado elecciones por la vivienda, sino que asegura que demasiada paciencia ha tenido la gente con este asunto: “No solo no me parece bien que se convoquen elecciones por este tema, sino que yo creo que ya estábamos tardando. Debería haber explotado hace muchísimo tiempo y que bastante paciencia ha tenido la gente con este asunto”, señala. A continuación, el comunicador de Mediaset ha apuntado los temas que debería decidir estas elecciones: “Dos cosas. Actualización de los sueldos. No puede ser que la gente esté ganando tan poco dinero. No se puede vivir con los salarios que se están pagando actualmente. Es imposible. Y luego solucionar inmediatamente de la manera que, como fuera, el tema de la vivienda”, sentencia. Finalmente, el de Badalona ha detallado la pregunta que le haría a uno de los candidatos del debate: “¿Prohibirías a los fondos buitre comprar vivienda en España para especular?”, afirmaba, asegurando que nunca podría ser el moderador en un debate de ese tipo porque “no dejaría hablar a Feijóo”.

articles.title: Mohanlal praises Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion': 'I am truly impressed with the way they have brought much-loved journey to a befitting end'
articles.summary: Praise from the actor who first brought a beloved character to life carries special meaning.
articles.body: Praise from the actor who first brought a beloved character to life carries special meaning. Mohanlal, who plays Georgekutty in the original Malayalam ‘Drishyam’ films, has watched the Hindi film ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ and shared his appreciation for how the story has been wrapped up. The Ajay Devgn starrer takes a different path from the Malayalam version, which makes the veteran actor’s response a big moment for the team.What Mohanlal said about the filmSharing a video, Mohanlal said, “I watched Drishyam: The Conclusion, and I am truly impressed with the way they have brought a much-loved journey to a befitting end. Congratulations to Abhishek Pathak, Kumar Mangat Pathak, Ajay Devgn and the entire cast and crew on a job so well done.”The Malayalam films have a loyal fan base, and Georgekutty remains one of the most memorable characters in Indian cinema. The Hindi franchise has chosen to move ahead in its own way instead of following the third Malayalam film. Several viewers have even said that the Hindi conclusion is better than the Malayalam one, which released earlier this year.A new story for the Hindi franchiseThe Hindi ‘Drishyam’ series began in 2015 as a remake of Jeethu Joseph’s Malayalam thriller. The first two films stayed close to the original, but ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ follows an original storyline made for the Hindi version.Speaking at FICCI Frames, Ajay Devgn said, “The original one they did not have Akshay Khanna’s character as such, but 3 is a completely new script. They are two very different films. The way Abhishek and the writers have worked so hard on the script for the past maybe two years that it really, really gives you a high. The way it has shaped up the scripting and the way Abhishek has made the film, I think it has come out fabulous. That’s when we decided that it should be the conclusion.”Strong run at the box officeThe film has done well in theatres too. ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ has reportedly earned over Rs 479.80 crore worldwide, while its India gross has crossed Rs 370.80 crore.Ajay Devgn, Tabu and Jaideep Ahlawat lead the castAjay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar, the family man known for outsmarting the police. Tabu is back as Meera Deshmukh, and Shriya Saran plays Nandini. The cast also includes Rajat Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat, Prakash Raj, Kamlesh Sawant, Ishita Dutta and Mrunal Jadhav.Jaideep Ahlawat plays SP Rajveer Singh Tomar, who poses a fresh challenge for Vijay. Their face-offs have caught the eye of viewers, and many on social media have praised Ahlawat as a strong addition to the franchise.Directed by Abhishek Pathak, the film was released in theatres on October 2, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2006, Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie established a foundation to support humanitarian causes; its work extended across several countries
articles.summary: In 2006, Hollywood actors Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie established the Jolie-Pitt Foundation to support humanitarian work and provide assistance to people
articles.body: In 2006, Hollywood actors Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie established the Jolie-Pitt Foundation to support humanitarian work and provide assistance to people facing difficult circumstances around the world. The foundation became their major charitable act, supporting numerous organizations dealing with issues of poverty, children, health care, and homeless people.Their interest in humanitarian issues was not limited to the film industry. Jolie worked for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees as a goodwill ambassador since 2001, and she was actively involved in many humanitarian projects. Her experiences during visits to areas affected by conflict and displacement helped bring international attention to the challenges faced by refugees and vulnerable families.The foundation’s work included supporting established organisations that provided direct assistance to people in crisis. In May 2007, the Jolie-Pitt Foundation donated US$1 million towards humanitarian efforts for people affected by the conflict in Sudan’s Darfur region. The contribution was directed to three organisations: UNHCR, the International Rescue Committee and SOS Children’s Villages. These organisations were involved in helping displaced people and supporting communities affected by the humanitarian emergency.One of the foundation’s significant initiatives came in September 2008, when it pledged US$2 million to support healthcare programmes in Ethiopia. The funding was intended to establish a centre in Addis Ababa for children affected by HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, along with a programme to treat tuberculosis in children and adults. The initiative built on the couple’s earlier support for the Maddox Chivan Children’s Center in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, which provided medical care, education and social services to children affected by HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis.Their charitable contributions also covered environmental protection, disaster recovery and support for children. According to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the foundation contributed to organisations and projects involved in rebuilding after Hurricane Katrina in the United States, supporting children’s health centres in Cambodia and Ethiopia, and protecting wildlife in Namibia. It also supported organisations including Doctors Without Borders and the Global Action for Children initiative.The Jolie-Pitt Foundation reflected the couple’s decision to use their resources to support work beyond the entertainment industry. Rather than limiting their contributions to one issue or region, they directed funding towards different humanitarian and environmental needs, working through organisations with experience in those areas.Their philanthropic efforts formed part of a broader history of public engagement with humanitarian causes, particularly Jolie’s longstanding work on behalf of refugees and displaced people.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sean "Diddy" Combs leaves prison after suffering head injury: Report
articles.summary: Diddy was taken for medical treatment after suffering a head injury at a federal prison, according to TMZ.
articles.body:
Sean "Diddy" Combs was transported from federal prison for medical treatment early Saturday after suffering a head injury, according to TMZ, while his representative told Newsweek that Combs' team was working to confirm the situation.

"We are aware of the reports concerning Sean Combs and are working to confirm the circumstances. Sean's health and well-being are our immediate concern, and we appreciate everyone who has reached out," the representative said Monday.

Sources at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey told TMZ that an ambulance carrying Combs left the prison grounds around 1 a.m. The outlet said it was unclear how Combs sustained the injury and that it had not confirmed whether he was taken to a hospital.

Combs was conscious and speaking when he was returned to the prison before sunrise, TMZ said.

The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to discuss Combs' medical status with Newsweek . "For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individual, including quarters assignment or medical status," the agency said in an email.

The reported medical incident follows shortly after an NBC News investigation into Combs' life at Fort Dix, citing four men who spent time in his unit, along with photos and videos the outlet reviewed. NBC reported allegations that Combs had access to contraband cellphones and alcohol and paid other inmates to perform tasks for him.

Combs' spokesperson downplayed the report, while the Bureau of Prisons declined to comment on his conditions. NBC subsequently reported that Combs was placed in solitary confinement following publication of the story.

Combs had previously been placed in solitary confinement following a fight with another inmate over the summer, NBC News reported in July.

Combs was found guilty in 2025 of transporting two women, identified in court as Cassie Ventura and "Jane," for the purpose of prostitution, violations of the Mann Act. He was acquitted of the more serious racketeering conspiracy and sex-trafficking charges.

The split verdict followed a closely watched federal trial in Manhattan. Prosecutors had accused Combs of operating a criminal enterprise and using his businesses and employees to facilitate sexual encounters, allegations that formed part of the government's broader racketeering case. The jury ultimately rejected the racketeering and sex-trafficking counts while convicting him on the two prostitution-related transportation charges.

Combs was sentenced to 50 months in federal prison, a $500,000 fine, and five years of supervised release. He appealed his sentence to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, arguing that the sentencing judge improperly relied on conduct connected to charges he had been acquitted of. The appeals court heard arguments on April 9, 2026, but did not immediately issue a ruling.

Separately, Combs faces dozens of lawsuits alleging misconduct. Those cases are proceeding independently of his federal criminal appeal, meaning the outcome of his challenge to the prison sentence would not itself resolve the civil claims against him.

Combs has a projected release date of March 2, 2028, according to Bureau of Prisons records. The date is subject to change and was recently pushed back from January 21, 2028.

Newsweek's reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here .

Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Samantha Beech and Sam Wilson .

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Florence Pugh: ‘You owe it to yourself to really work out who you are,’ a powerful life lesson on self-awareness and finding your potential
articles.summary: Florence Pugh inspires self-awareness and personal growth in her quote, emphasizing the importance of understanding oneself and overcoming internal fears. Learn how her journey in acting reflects this powerful life lesson.
articles.body: There are some things in life that are completely out of your hands. You can prepare for a job interview and still not get the job. You can give an audition everything you have and still not get the role. You can work hard and still have someone else make the final decision. But then there are the things that are actually up to you.Knowing the difference can save you a lot of unnecessary worrying. Florence Pugh has spoken about this while discussing her career, the fear that comes with taking on difficult roles and why she does not want to keep doing the same thing just because she already knows she can do it.Today’s quote of the day by Florence Pugh reads: “I think you owe it to yourself to really work out who you are, what you are capable of, and, more to the point, what will hold you back.”Pugh shared this thought in her interview with STRIPLV, while discussing fear, uncertainty and her approach to acting. She explained that if something is outside your control, such as whether you will be cast in a movie, you should still do everything possible to give yourself the best chance. But if the thing holding you back is within your control, such as fear, she believes it is your responsibility to deal with it.What does the quote by Florence Pugh mean?The Florence Pugh quote is basically about being honest with yourself. It is easy to blame circumstances when something does not work out. Sometimes, of course, circumstances really are the problem. You cannot control another person's decision.What you can control is how prepared you are, how much effort you put in and whether you let fear stop you before you have even tried.That distinction was important to Pugh. In the same STRIPLV interview, she talked about how fear in acting is often connected to the future. Once the cameras are actually rolling, that fear can disappear. Realising that, she said, can make you more willing to take on bigger challenges.And that is probably the most relatable part of this motivational quote. Sometimes you are not actually afraid of doing something. You are afraid of what might happen if you do it.How is the quote by Florence Pugh relevant today?There is a lot of pressure to have your life figured out early. You are expected to know what career you want, what you are good at and where you are going.But you only really learn those things by trying. Pugh's approach to acting is a good example. She said she could not imagine being considered only for the same kinds of characters throughout her career. She wanted to keep testing herself and working with different filmmakers.That does not mean every risk will pay off. It means you should at least give yourself the chance.Maybe you want to apply for a job you think is slightly above your level. Maybe you want to start writing, audition for something, launch a small business or simply do something you have always been too nervous to try. The result is not completely in your control. Trying is.And sometimes that is enough reason to start.Early life of Florence PughFlorence Pugh was born on January 3, 1996, in Oxford, England. She grew up in a family with creative interests and spent part of her childhood in Spain before returning to England.She became interested in acting while she was young and eventually began pursuing it professionally. Her early career wasn't the typical overnight success story. Instead, she gained attention through challenging performances and slowly moved into larger projects.How did Florence Pugh rise to fame?Pugh made her film debut in 'The Falling' in 2014, playing Abbie Mortimer. The performance immediately put her on the radar of critics and filmmakers.She followed it with roles in 'Lady Macbeth' and 'Outlaw King', before reaching a much wider audience with 'Little Women' in 2019. Her performance as Amy March earned her an Academy Award nomination.Then came 'Midsommar', 'Black Widow', 'Don't Worry Darling', 'A Good Person' and 'Oppenheimer'. She also joined the 'Dune' franchise with 'Dune: Part Two'.What stands out about Pugh's career is the variety. She has moved between intimate dramas, psychological films, superhero movies and huge blockbusters instead of sticking to one formula. That fits closely with what she told STRIPLV about wanting to keep testing herself.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Selma Blair Arrested After Allegedly Biting Flight Attendant and Trying to Open Plane Door; Rep Says She Suffered ‘Medical Emergency’
articles.summary: Selma Blair was arrested on Sunday after an alleged violent incident on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York, Variety has confirmed. The “Legally Blon...
articles.body:
Selma Blair was arrested on Sunday after an alleged violent incident on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York, Variety has confirmed.

The "Legally Blonde" actress allegedly punched one flight attendant and bit another after attempting to open the plane door while in the air, per TMZ. Law enforcement was parked at the gate and responded to the incident once the aircraft landed in in New York, where the 54-year-old Blair was taken into custody and transported to a hospital for evaluation. Two flight attendants reported injuries, with one receiving care at a hospital.

A representative for Blair told TMZ: "Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."

The Port Authority confirmed Blair's identity to Variety . A source says the FBI is currently investigating the incident.

In a statement to Variety , a Delta Airlines spokesperson said, "Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first."

Despite the chaos on board, there was no operational impact to the flight, which landed at John F. Kennedy airport at approximately 11 p.m., ahead of schedule.

This is not the first time Blair has experienced an outburst on a plane. In 2016, she was removed from a flight on a stretcher while traveling with her 4-year-old son after she "had a total psychotic blackout." Blair chalked up the incident to drinking a glass of wine and taking a pill, saying at the time, "It was horrible and frightening and I had empathy for myself actually afterwards because it was actually so out of character for me, especially because I'm a mother."

articles.title: Judge Judy credits Her Honor program with making her 'hopeful' for the next generation
articles.summary: Judge Judy Sheindlin's Her Honor Mentoring program celebrates 20 years of empowering young women through mentorship and financial literacy skills.
articles.body: Judge Judy Sheindlin recently announced that she’s "rewiring" and letting son Adam Levy take the reins of TV courtroom drama, but she has plenty of other projects to keep her busy. The Her Honor Mentoring program she helped co-found just celebrated its 20-year anniversary. Sheindlin founded the program with her daughter Nicole Sheindlin to empower young women through mentorship and professional development. For the past two decades, Her Honor Mentoring has welcomed approximately 2,500 participants; 1,500 mentees, selected from 31 high schools across the region, and more than 1,000 mentors from 400 organizations and businesses. "I’m so happy to be here 20 years after our freshman year," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital. The project, she said, "started off with a dream" and all they could do was hope it was successful. The first class held only eight or nine women, whereas the most recent class in September saw over 100. JUDGE JUDY SHARES THE BEST PIECE OF PROFESSIONAL ADVICE SHE EVER RECEIVED AHEAD OF HER HONOR EVENT "It’s the combination of the mentoring and the financial part of it – which is the girls get paid for working… and learning how to dress for success, learning about making first impressions, learning how to manage your money and just knowing how to grow up financially prepared to be an adult," Sheindlin told Fox News Digital. The project, she said, is "simple, but satisfying." And she's been impressed and inspired by the young participants' drive to succeed. "This small cohort makes me hopeful," Sheindlin said. "I think that you become jaded when you see so much dysfunction. I’ve been around so much adult dysfunction and juvenile dysfunction, that to see young people still hoping and dreaming, wanting to work hard to realize their dream that their journey on this Earth is positive and fulfilling, makes you feel good. It sort of renews your faith that probably the vast majority of people are like these young women. That they want their lives to be productive and happy and fulfilling." Several of the former mentees have come back as mentors after starting their careers. "We’re teaching them to give back," she said. "We’re teaching these young women the importance of being not only for themselves. But then once you’ve realized that, to supporting others with your time and your talent… they have a drive, they want to be their own engines. They want to be the engine that pulls their own train." MORE GEN Z COLLEGE FRESHMEN ARE QUITTING SCHOOL EARLY AND MOVING BACK HOME WITH MOM AND DAD JUDGE ADAM LEVY PREVIEWS HIS ‘NITTY-GRITTY’ NEW SHOW – AND HOW HIS STYLE COMPARES TO HIS MOM JUDGE JUDY Sheindlin credited her stepdaughter Nicole as being "the engine that keeps the project running." Nicole, the current CEO of Her Honor Mentoring, said the program started as a reflection of her relationship with Judge Judy. She went to the same law school as her stepmother and sat on the bench with her when she was a judge in family court. Nicole called it the perfect model for the program, saying, "The power and the impact of having a professional woman, a strong woman be a mentor, be a guide, be a supporter." The mother-daughter duo concluded they should empower young women together to help women gain some extra skills and expand their professional network. "We’ve come to learn how much the mentors have grown and are inspired," Nicole told Fox Digital. "They’ve discovered that giving back empowers their own personal wellbeing." The program connects mentees with mentors across several industries. During 20 weekly meetings throughout the academic year, mentoring teams explore topics related to education, career and financial literacy. In addition, as part of the Her Honor experience, mentees complete four electives. The offerings include field trips, digital courses and creative projects. JUDGE JUDY HAS SCATHING MESSAGE FOR CITIES ENGULFED IN BRAZEN CRIME, PINPOINTS ‘RIDICULOUS’ POLICIES' The 2026-27 Her Honor class consists of 108 mentees and 123 mentors across 14 schools throughout Bronx, Rockland and Westchester counties. Mentee Keiry Alvarez and her mentor Lilliana Mendoza said they were grateful that the program helped them overcome their timidity. Alvarez, who said she was encouraged to join the program after her sister said Her Honor has helped her become more confident and outspoken. Mendoza was the first generation female to go to college in her family and a 2016 Her Honor mentee. She said the program helped her combat her shyness, gain people skills and find her voice. She added that it gave her specific guidance that has made an impact on her career as a police officer in the Mamaroneck Police Department. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Throughout my mentorship, I learned to have a lot of empathy for people and understand how people are, and I think that was a big part, because I also have a lot of empathy for people," she told Fox Digital.

articles.title: Selma Blair taken into custody after being physically abusive on Delta flight, officials say
articles.summary: Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital after the flight landed in New York, the New York port authority said.
articles.body: Selma Blair was taken into custody after she was physically abusive on a Delta Air Lines flight traveling from Los Angeles to New York City on Sunday, according to a spokesperson for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. Blair, 54, the “Cruel Intentions” actor, was identified as the suspect by the Port Authority, which said she was taken to a hospital for evaluation after the flight landed at John F. Kennedy International Airport. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, the spokesperson said. The spokesperson provided no additional details about what happened on the aircraft but said the FBI is investigating. The FBI confirmed it was responsible for investigating all incidents aboard aircraft and said it had been contacted regarding a “potential assault aboard a flight that arrived into JFK.” “As per long-standing DOJ policy, we do not comment on ongoing investigations,” the FBI said. The Federal Aviation Administration also said it would investigate a “passenger disturbance” on the flight. A representative for Blair confirmed in a statement that she was taken to the hospital following the flight. “Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct,” the representative said. “Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition.” Blair’s representative did not describe the medical emergency. Blair revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disorder that attacks healthy cells in the central nervous system, according to the National Institutes of Health. Delta did not identify Blair in response to a request for comment and said it has “zero tolerance” for unlawful behavior in a statement Monday. “The safety of our customers and crew always comes first,” it said. Blair had an incident on a plane in 2016 involving her having a verbal outburst accusing someone of wanting to kill her, TMZ reported at the time. She was taken off the flight on a stretcher and transported to a hospital when the flight landed in Los Angeles. She later admitted having mixed alcohol and medication in a statement to Vanity Fair, apologizing for her behavior. “I take this very seriously, and I apologize to all of the passengers and crew that I disturbed and am thankful to all of the people who helped me in the aftermath,” Blair said at the time. “I am a flawed human being who makes mistakes and am filled with shame over this incident.”

articles.title: Shane Gillis’ ‘SNL’ monologue slammed as sexist for comments about women
articles.summary: The comedian drew criticism online after he said women at the gym “just dress like whores now.”
articles.body: Comedian Shane Gillis drew controversy again for his “Saturday Night Live” monologue Saturday after commenting that he “didn’t know women just dress like whores now” at the gym. Gillis appeared to draw few laughs from the studio audience after making the remark during the monologue, which marked his third time hosting the NBC sketch comedy show. (“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.) After lamenting that he needs to lose weight, he went on to describe the “neon, artificial-vape colored” shorts that women are wearing to work out, and the fact that men are not allowed to look at women in those shorts. The bit drew an outpouring of backlash toward Gillis online, with hundreds of people sharing their negative reactions on TikTok, Instagram, X and Threads. Representatives for “SNL” and Gillis did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Gillis, who is known for his raunchy style of comedy, has a history of placing women — and other marginalized groups — at the butt of jokes. Many people called it tone-deaf of Gillis to make such comments following the reports around a former Cornell University student who alleged she was gang-raped at an on-campus fraternity house in 2024. Among the chorus of vocal critics was actor Dan Levy, who on Sunday posted an Instagram video in which he said, “Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists. There’s a difference there.” Levy, who created and starred in “Schitt’s Creek,” said he is “speechless that something like that can exist on live national television.” “And to be perfectly honest,” Levy continued, “more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment with which women are sexually assaulted, and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a crime.” Levy called on men to defend women more often and said it is not a women’s issue — “this is an everybody issue,” he added. “The more that men objectify women in the media, the more that other men see them as objects and treat them as objects,” he said. “They are not objects. They are superior human beings to men.” Some used Gillis’ monologue to show solidarity for Cornell’s Jane Doe, who accused seven Chi Phi fraternity members of plying her with drugs before sexually assaulting her overnight following a fraternity party. As the investigation made headlines, women began sharing their own experiences with sexual assault on campus and what they say were inadequate responses from their universities and their police departments, with some coalescing around the hashtag #iamjanedoe. Writer Jessica Valenti said that she thinks Gillis was probably aware about the “major national conversation happening right now about sexual assault” in relation to the Cornell case. “This is his contribution to that conversation,” she said. “This is him telling us what he thinks of the discourse on sexual assault. ... That is rape culture.” Others, like writer and comedian Sophia Benoit, said Gillis’ joke about how women dress at the gym was not funny. It “has been a very common joke for AT LEAST fifteen years, and it has never once that I can recall been performed with a punchline,” she wrote on X. Gillis’ career has been fraught with controversy, mainly, his time with “SNL.” He was hired as a cast member in 2019, before he was quickly canned for previously making racist jokes on his podcast. The criticisms of Gillis piled on when other clips of him using offensive language went viral at the time. At the time, he apologized but said he would continue to make shocking and taboo jokes. “We want SNL to have a variety of voices and points of view within the show, and we hired Shane on the strength of his talent as a comedian and his impressive audition for SNL,” a spokesperson for “SNL” executive producer Lorne Michaels told NBC News in 2019. “We were not aware of his prior remarks that have surfaced over the past few days. The language he used is offensive, hurtful and unacceptable.” The show, which was home to Bowen Yang (the show’s first Asian American cast member) at the time, chose to fire Gillis, but invited him back to host in 2024 and 2025 before Saturday’s appearance. Later during Saturday’s episode, Gillis accidentally slipped an f-bomb during a sketch and later apologized. The Federal Communications Commission “prohibits obscene, indecent and profane content from being broadcast on the radio or TV.” The agency defines “profane content” as “grossly offensive” language that is “considered a public nuisance,” according to its website. Some online pointed out that Gillis apologized for cursing during a sketch but not for offending people during his monologue. “That’s a pretty ridiculous contrast,” one social media user wrote. “An accidental swear gets an apology, while insulting women is supposed to pass as edgy comedy.”

images.caption: Shane Gillis during his monologue on "Saturday Night Live" on Oct. 10, 2026.

articles.title: Harry Styles addresses ICE shooting in New York with call for ‘dignity and justice’
articles.summary: Harry Styles urged Madison Square Garden fans to show compassion and justice for Oscar Belgal after the ICE shooting sparked protests in New York City.
articles.body: Harry Styles paused his concert at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday to address the shooting of a Dominican immigrant by federal immigration agents, urging fans to show compassion toward people from different backgrounds and calling for "dignity" and "justice." The British pop star addressed the crowd after referencing Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old man who was shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers Thursday while his 5-year-old son was sitting in the back seat of his car. "I just want us to take a moment to think about Oscar Belgal tonight, and I want us to think and remember to just look after each other," Styles said. "So, please, continue looking after each other," he continued. "And remember, your friends, the people you love, the people who don't look like you and aren't born where you're from, they deserve respect, and love, and dignity and justice." PARAMORE'S HAYLEY WILLIAMS LAUNCHES VULGAR TIRADE AT DHS AFTER AGENCY DEFENDS ICE OFFICERS The remarks prompted criticism from film critic and commentator Christian Toto, who told Fox News Digital that speaking out against ICE has become a way for celebrities to gain approval within the entertainment industry. "This is the new black square on Instagram — speaking out on ICE gets you respect within your artistic community and endless positive press," Toto said. "I think the mainstream media has far more impact on public opinion. Social media does, too. Celebrities weighing in on matters like this? I suspect it doesn't move the needle at all. We view the stars as detached from our day-to-day lives, so we may agree with them on hot-button issues but they're not winning any converts." He suggested that entertainers face pressure within Hollywood to embrace political causes, while those who remain silent may be better positioned to avoid alienating fans. "There's an expectation within celebrity circles to embrace the cause du jour. The benefits are clear, and they're never held responsible when history doesn't align with their views. I suspect the stars who don't speak out at all fare best with their fans," Toto said. OLIVIA WILDE BREAKS SILENCE ON HARRY STYLES FANS AND THEIR BRUTAL REACTION TO THEIR 10-YEAR AGE GAP ROMANCE Styles' comments came as the shooting of Belgal sparked protests and criticism from New York officials, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Belgal was shot after allegedly refusing to comply with officers conducting a targeted arrest operation, Fox News Digital reported. Federal officials said he accelerated his vehicle toward agents, prompting them to open fire. During a Thursday night news conference, Mamdani said he personally urged Trump to release Belgal and condemned the federal immigration agency. "We know that ICE is rotten to its core. Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known..." Mamdani said. MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED' Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, defended the shooting during a Friday news conference alongside Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, saying officers believed their lives were in danger. "Our officers, using their training and believing that their life and the life of the partners and the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," Charles said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Officials said agents were unaware that Belgal's son was inside the vehicle. The child was unharmed. The Department of Homeland Security said Belgal had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests for assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. Federal officials also alleged ties to the Trinitarios street gang. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A federal judge temporarily blocked Belgal's deportation Friday while his legal challenge to detention proceeds, and the New York Police Department released body camera footage showing the aftermath of the shooting.

articles.title: RJ Mitte, ‘Breaking Bad’ actor who played Walter White Jr., dies at 34
articles.summary: Actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte, who played Walter "Flynn" White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died at age 34.
articles.body: RJ Mitte, the actor who played Walter White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died. "It is with profound sadness we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," Mitte's representative told Fox News Digital. "RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad. Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement continued. "Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s." The statement noted that Mitte also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, which supports philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities. Mitte’s cause of death was not immediately disclosed. Like his character on the Emmy Award-winning show, Mitte had cerebral palsy and was a disability rights advocate. Mitte appeared on "The Joe Vulpis Podcast" last week and spoke about how "Breaking Bad" changed his life and on his close relationship with the cast years after the show's finale, TMZ reported. This story is breaking. Please check back for updates.

articles.title: In 2001, Nicolas Cage declined the role of Aragorn in ‘The Lord of the Rings’ to stay closer to his family: 'I didn't want to go away for three years...needed to be home with my son'
articles.summary: In a candid reflection, Nicolas Cage reveals he turned down the role of Aragorn in 'The Lord of the Rings' to prioritize family time with his son, Weston. Discover the actor's insights into his decision and how it shaped his career.
articles.body: Nicolas Cage could have been part of one of the biggest fantasy franchises in Hollywood history. He was considered for Aragorn in 'The Lord of the Rings', the role that eventually went to Viggo Mortensen. But Cage had a reason for stepping away from the opportunity, and it had little to do with the character or the films themselves.He did not want to spend years away from home while his son, Weston, was growing up. Looking back, the actor has made it clear that being there for his family mattered more than taking on another major film franchise.Why Nicolas Cage passed on 'The Lord of the Rings'Nicolas Cage discussed the missed role in a 2015 interview with Newsweek, where he named Aragorn when talking about projects he had turned down. “There were different things going on in my life at the time that precluded me from being able to travel and be away from home for three years,” he said.The actor also explained that he had no problem enjoying the films as a viewer. In fact, he spoke about being able to watch 'The Lord of the Rings' without wondering what his own performance might have looked like. “I don't really have any regrets. Regret is a waste of time,” Cage said in the interview, reflecting on the roles that never became part of his filmography.It is an unusually relaxed way to talk about missing out on a franchise that went on to become a global phenomenon. Cage did not frame the decision as a career disaster. He had his reasons, and he was comfortable with them.His son Weston was the reason behind the decisionNicolas Cage explained the family side of the story more directly in an interview with PEOPLE in 2022, while discussing 'The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent'. “There’s no version of Nic Cage in reality that doesn’t want to spend time with his children,” he said. He went on to explain that family had always come before his career.“I turned down Lord of the Rings, and I turned down Matrix because I didn’t want to go to New Zealand for three years or Australia for three years because I needed to be home with my son Weston; that’s a fact.”The comment also revealed that 'The Lord of the Rings' was not the only major franchise Cage passed on for family reasons. He turned down 'The Matrix' as well, which would have required an extended commitment in Australia.Weston, Cage's eldest son with actor Christina Fulton, was still a child during the period when the films were being made. The prospect of being away for long stretches was clearly something Cage took seriously.Viggo Mortensen became the Aragorn audiences knowPeter Jackson's 'The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring' arrived in cinemas on 19 December 2001, with Viggo Mortensen playing Aragorn, the ranger who gradually embraces his role as the heir to Gondor's throne.Mortensen's performance became a defining part of the trilogy. For many fans, it is now difficult to picture anyone else carrying Aragorn's quiet strength, his loyalty to the Fellowship and his reluctance to claim the throne before he is ready.Nicolas Cage's casting story remains an interesting Hollywood what-if, but there is no need to turn it into a tale of regret. His own comments suggest he can appreciate the films without wishing he had been in them.A Hollywood role he chose not to takeNicolas Cage has spent his career moving between big studio films, independent projects and roles that are anything but predictable. Passing on 'The Lord of the Rings' did not stop him from building a distinctive career, and he has never suggested that the decision ruined his chances of success. Sometimes a casting story is about the role an actor lost. This one is also about what he chose to keep: time with his son.For fans, imagining Cage as Aragorn may always be an intriguing exercise. But the actor's explanation is straightforward. A lengthy shoot overseas would have meant being away from Weston for years, and Cage wanted to be home. articles.title: The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
articles.summary: Aaron Sorkin’s followup to The Social Network is a box office dud, but Other Mommy is apparently a hit.
articles.body: As important as some of the messages in The Social Reckoning are, the movie has been drastically underperforming at the box office. Per Variety, Aaron’s Sorkin’s follow up to The Social Network only grossed a measly $5.5 million this past weekend against a budget that’s somewhere within the $30–42 million range. That would make it a certifiable flop that’s costing Columbia Pictures (and Sony) quite a bit of money — especially when you compare it to The Social Network’s $22 million opening. This isn’t entirely surprising given how middling reviews for the film have been. It’s currently got a 55% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and has widely been trashed on social media. All of this might be reflective of audiences hoping for a proper sequel to The Social Network, which won three Oscars for its screenplay (written by Sorkin), editing, and score. But it might speak to people not fully clicking with Mikey Madison’s performance as whistleblower Frances Haugen or Jeremy Allen White’s turn as Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz. (Madison, for her part, indicated to The Hollywood Reporter that it was Sorkin’s vision as director that kept from “authentically and faithfully represent[ing] a real person,” which she hopes to do in the future.) It also probably didn’t help that Jesse Eisenberg — who portrayed Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network — had no interest in being in the film, according to Sorkin himself. Ironically, Blumhouse’s Other Mommy raked in an impressive $27.5 million this weekend, which likely suggests that people are more interested in novel horror as opposed to reminders of how social media has made everyone’s lives worse.

articles.title: Muere a los 34 años RJ Mitte, el actor que interpretó al hijo de Walter White en 'Breaking Bad'
articles.standfirst: El actor, que tenía parálisis cerebral leve desde su nacimiento, fue también un destacado activista por los derechos de las personas con discapacidad
articles.summary: El actor, que tenía parálisis cerebral leve desde su nacimiento, fue también un destacado activista por los derechos de las personas con discapacidad
articles.body: El actor RJ Mitte, conocido por interpretar a Walter White Jr., el hijo del protagonista de la aclamada serie 'Breaking Bad', ha muerto a los 34 años en Brownsville, Texas, según informaron sus representantes. El fallecimiento del actor ha sido comunicado a través de un mensaje en el que han destacado su faceta artística y su compromiso social. Por el momento, no se ha hecho pública la causa de su muerte. "Con profunda tristeza compartimos la noticia del trágico fallecimiento de RJ Mitte, querido actor, filántropo y apasionado defensor de los derechos de las personas con discapacidad", han apuntado sus representantes en el comunicado. Nacido con parálisis cerebral leve, RJ Mitte convirtió su experiencia personal en una herramienta para promover la inclusión y defender los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Su participación en 'Breaking Bad' tuvo un significado especial, ya que su personaje también padecía parálisis cerebral, una circunstancia que contribuyó a dar visibilidad a esta condición en una de las producciones televisivas más reconocidas de los últimos años. A través de su popularidad, el actor estadounidense impulsó iniciativas de concienciación y reivindicó una representación más inclusiva de las personas con discapacidad en la industria audiovisual y en la sociedad. RJ Mitte alcanzó la popularidad internacional gracias a 'Breaking Bad', la serie protagonizada por Bryan Cranston en el papel de Walter White, un profesor de química que comienza a fabricar metanfetamina tras ser diagnosticado de cáncer. La ficción, emitida entre 2008 y 2013, se convirtió en un fenómeno televisivo y recibió numerosos reconocimientos por su guion, sus interpretaciones y su desarrollo narrativo. La producción acumuló 58 nominaciones a los premios Emmy en horario estelar y obtuvo 16 galardones, entre ellos dos premios a la mejor serie dramática. La trayectoria de RJ Mitte quedó estrechamente vinculada a 'Breaking Bad', una de las series más premiadas de la televisión estadounidense, y a su labor en favor de los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Su interpretación de Walter White Jr. contribuyó a visibilizar la parálisis cerebral en la ficción televisiva.

articles.title: ‘Breaking Bad’ actor RJ Mitte passes away at 34; disability rights advocate dies by suicide: Reports
articles.summary: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains references to suicide.
articles.body: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains references to suicide. Actor RJ Mitte, best known for playing Walter White Jr., aka Flynn, in the hit television series ‘Breaking Bad’, has sadly passed away. He was 34.According to a TMZ report, county officials have reportedly confirmed that the actor passed away in Texas on Monday. His death is being investigated as a suicide, with law enforcement officials confirming that the investigation was ongoing.In a statement shared with TMZ, Mitte’s representatives expressed profound sadness over his death, describing him as a beloved actor, philanthropist and passionate disability rights advocate. "Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," his reps said and continued, "Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s."Mitte appeared in 56 episodes of AMC’s award-winning series ‘Breaking Bad’, in which he played the son of Bryan Cranston’s Walter White.Mitte most recently made a public appearance on ‘The Joe Vulpis Podcast’, where he spoke about how ‘Breaking Bad’ had changed his life and discussed his bond with the cast, years after the series finale. Earlier this month, he also reunited with his co-star Luis Moncada, with the two appearing cheerful in social media posts.Apart from ‘Breaking Bad’, Mitte was known for his work in projects including ‘The Oak Room’, ‘The Recall’ and ‘The Guardians of Justice (Will Save You!)’.On the personal front, the actor was engaged to Kennedy Suarez, whom he had been dating for several years. He proposed to her last year.Beyond acting, Mitte served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s. He also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, supporting philanthropic initiatives and community programmes while challenging stereotypes surrounding people with disabilities. In 2019, Mitte spoke about the need for greater representation of disabled actors in Hollywood, highlighting the importance of creating more opportunities for performers with disabilities.His representatives have requested, "At this time, we ask people to respect the privacy of RJ Mitte’s family and close ones."DISCLAIMER: If you or someone you know is struggling with suicidal thoughts, anxiety, depression, mental illness, domestic violence, assault, or abuse, please seek immediate help from a doctor, mental health expert, NGO, or trusted individual.
